note: 'Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up,' (John 3:14) -- the lifting up is the stated ground, not the serpent itself.

'Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness ... He gave them bread from heaven to eat' (John 6:31), answered with 'I am the bread of life' (John 6:35). Paul calls the same manna 'spiritual meat' at 1Cor 10:3 without saying what it stands for, so the key is John's.

'our fathers were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; and were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea' (1Cor 10:1-2). Paul reads the crossing as a baptism; the cloud is the pillar that went before them and stood between them and Egypt.

'all passed through the sea; They were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea' (1Cor 10:1-2). Paul says only 'the sea'; that it is the Red Sea is the graph's step and not his. Exod 14:22 has Israel pass through on dry ground and calls it only 'the sea'; Exod 15:4 names the Red sea for the same crossing.
'they drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ.' (1Cor 10:4). The plainest key in the corpus, and Paul states it outright rather than by comparison.
